name: Suminagashi
author: E. T. Carter
description: Japanese floating-ink marbling on warm fibred paper: nests of thin concentric ink rings grow around three drop points, flatten one another where they meet, and are drawn out by a stylus into long feathered tongues with a fine comb ripple laid across them. Two inks only, a warm sumi black and one colour, thinning where the water pulled them.

params.label: Rings
params.effect: Drops per nest; low is a few bold rings with paper between, high packs each nest with fine hairlines.

params.label: Ring spacing
params.effect: Spacing between rings; low is a dense nest of hairlines, high spreads a few wide rings across the sheet.

params.label: Stylus draw
params.effect: How far the stylus pulls the rings into drawn-out tongues; 0 leaves the nests round.

params.label: Fanning
params.effect: Amplitude of the fanned waves that feather every line; 0 is calm concentric rings.

params.label: Water
params.effect: Speed of the water: the breath ripple, the drifting fan and stylus lines and the wandering drop points; 0 stills the surface.
